title: September 2021 Class College Final Supplementary Exam (Part 6 of 6)
unit: Comprehensive Nursing (HIV, Community Health, Public Health, Education, Infectious Diseases, Management)

sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the September 2021 class College Final Supplementary Exam paper (Kenya Registered Nursing, sat 30 May 2024, Multiple Choice Questions, Q101 to Q120).

questions.text: To prevent HIV positive patients from malaria, toxoplasmosis infection they are covered using:
questions.explanation: Cotrimoxazole (A) is correct because cotrimoxazole preventive therapy (CPT) is given to people living with HIV to prevent Pneumocystis pneumonia, toxoplasmosis, bacterial infections and malaria, and it is started in all people with HIV in line with the Kenya guidelines (960 mg daily for adults). Isoniazid therapy (B) is incorrect because isoniazid preventive therapy prevents tuberculosis. Sulfadoxine pyrimethamine (C) is incorrect because it is given as intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in pregnancy, but it must not be used with cotrimoxazole because of the risk of adverse effects. Acyclovir (D) is incorrect because it is an antiviral for herpes simplex and zoster.

questions.text: The form of abuse likely to happen to the elderly persons in the community is:
questions.explanation: Psychological (D) is the best answer because emotional or psychological abuse (insults, threats, isolation, humiliation, neglect of the emotional needs and the loss of respect and decision-making) is the commonest form of elder abuse reported in the community and is often hidden, and it includes verbal abuse. Physical (A) and sexual (B) abuse are incorrect because they are less common and are usually reported in institutions. Verbal (C) is incorrect as the best answer because it is only one part of psychological abuse. Note: this item is open to interpretation (neglect and financial abuse are also common), so check it against the marking scheme.

questions.text: In the integrated waste management hierarchy, the best method of solid waste management is:
questions.explanation: Reduce (B) is correct because the waste hierarchy ranks the options from the most to the least preferred: reduce (prevent waste at the source), reuse, recycle, recover (energy), and last treatment and disposal (incineration and landfill), since not producing the waste avoids all the costs and harm. Reuse (A) and recycle (C) are incorrect because they come second and third. Incinerate (D) is incorrect because it is a disposal method near the bottom of the hierarchy, and causes air pollution if not properly done.

questions.text: Ideal degrees to store vaccines at the health center level is:
questions.explanation: +2 to +8 (A) is correct because most vaccines (for example pentavalent, pneumococcal, rotavirus, measles-rubella, BCG and tetanus toxoid) are kept in the refrigerator at +2 to +8 degrees Celsius, and the temperature is checked twice a day with a thermometer and recorded on a temperature chart. -4 to +4 (B) and 0 to -4 (C) are incorrect because below 0 degrees the freeze-sensitive vaccines (such as pentavalent, TT and hepatitis B) are damaged. -10 to -25 (D) is incorrect because it is the freezer range, used at the national and regional stores for oral polio vaccine and for making ice packs, and not at the health center fridge. Use the shake test to check for freezing damage.

questions.text: Herd immunity is best maintained at:
questions.explanation: 95% (B) is correct because herd (community) immunity protects unvaccinated people when a high proportion of the population is immune, which stops the spread of the infectious agent, and the level that is needed depends on how infectious the disease is (about 80 to 85% for polio and about 95% for measles, the most infectious). 100% (A) is incorrect because it is not practically achievable. 85% (C) and 75% (D) are incorrect because they are too low for highly infectious diseases such as measles. Note: the threshold differs between diseases, but 95% is the figure usually taught as the best coverage to maintain.

questions.text: The primary health care principle that states that those with most needs are apportioned the highest number of resources is:
questions.explanation: Equity (C) is correct because equitable distribution means that health services and resources are shared according to need (the underserved, the poor and the vulnerable, such as remote rural areas, get more), so that everyone has a fair chance to attain the best health. Appropriate technology (A) is incorrect because it means methods that are scientifically sound, acceptable, affordable and locally maintainable. Intersectoral approach (B) is incorrect because it means collaboration between the health sector and other sectors (agriculture, education, water). Community participation (D) is incorrect because it means involving the people in planning, running and controlling their own health care.

questions.text: A true statement regarding school health activities is:

options.A: Its organized by the community member who then approach the community health nurse
options.B: It’s the sole mandate of health centers
options.C: It is an example of a static health delivery point
options.D: It serves all schools within a community health nurse catchment area

questions.explanation: It serves all schools within a community health nurse catchment area (D) is correct because the school health programme is planned and carried out by the health workers of the area (with the teachers and the education officers) for all the schools (public and private) in their catchment, and includes health education, screening, deworming, immunisation, first aid, and the promotion of sanitation. Organised by community members who approach the nurse (A) is incorrect because it is organised by the health team together with the schools. Sole mandate of health centers (B) is incorrect because it is a joint mandate of the health and education sectors. A static health delivery point (C) is incorrect because it is an outreach service, delivered at the school and not at the health facility.

questions.text: Vitamin B12 deficiency leads to:
questions.explanation: Pernicious anaemia (A) is correct because vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is needed for DNA synthesis in the red cell precursors, and its deficiency causes megaloblastic (macrocytic) anaemia, with neurological signs such as numbness and tingling, and a sore tongue. Scurvy (B) is incorrect because it is caused by vitamin C deficiency. Beriberi (C) is incorrect because it is caused by thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency. Pellagra (D) is incorrect because it is caused by niacin (vitamin B3) deficiency (dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia).

questions.text: The early neonatal death rate is expressed as:

options.A: A percentage of all live born infants

questions.explanation: Per 1000 live born deliveries (C) is correct because the early neonatal mortality rate is the number of deaths of live-born babies in the first 7 days of life per 1000 live births in the same period. A percentage of all live born infants (A) is incorrect because it is not the unit used. Per 1000 total deliveries (B) is incorrect because that unit (live births plus stillbirths) is used for the perinatal mortality rate. Per 100 000 deliveries (D) is incorrect because it is the unit for the maternal mortality ratio (per 100 000 live births).

questions.text: Educational objectives are described in:
questions.explanation: Three domains (B) is correct because Bloom's taxonomy classifies educational objectives into three domains: the cognitive domain (knowledge and thinking), the affective domain (attitudes, values and feelings) and the psychomotor domain (practical and motor skills). Two, four and five domains (A, C, D) are incorrect because they do not match the classification.

questions.text: A characteristic of learning is:

options.B: Results in temporary change in behavior

questions.explanation: Usually a continuous process (C) is correct because learning goes on throughout life, in formal and informal settings, with new knowledge built on prior experience, and it results in a relatively permanent change in behaviour. Mainly takes place in classrooms (A) is incorrect because it takes place anywhere (at home, at work, in the community, in the clinical area). Results in temporary change in behaviour (B) is incorrect because the change is relatively permanent. Always directly observable (D) is incorrect because some learning, such as a change in attitude or knowledge, is not directly visible and is inferred from performance.

questions.text: Puncture, Aspiration, Injection and Reaspiration (PAIR), is performed as surgical intervention for:
questions.explanation: Echinococcosis (C) is correct because PAIR is a percutaneous, ultrasound-guided treatment of hydatid cysts of Echinococcus granulosus, usually in the liver: the cyst is punctured, the fluid is aspirated, a scolicidal agent (such as hypertonic saline or alcohol) is injected and then re-aspirated, with albendazole cover to prevent spillage and anaphylaxis. Taeniasis (A) is incorrect because it is the intestinal tapeworm infection treated with praziquantel or niclosamide. Leishmaniasis (B) is incorrect because it is treated with antimonials or amphotericin. Schistosomiasis (D) is incorrect because it is treated with praziquantel.

questions.text: In TB management, optic neuritis is associated with:
questions.explanation: Ethambutol (B) is correct because it can cause dose-related optic neuritis (blurred vision, loss of visual acuity and red-green colour blindness), so the patient is told to report any visual change at once, and visual acuity and colour vision are checked before and during treatment. Pyrazinamide (A) is incorrect because it causes hyperuricaemia, arthralgia and hepatitis. Rifampicin (C) is incorrect because it causes orange discolouration of body fluids and hepatitis. Isoniazid (D) is incorrect because it causes peripheral neuropathy (prevented by pyridoxine) and hepatitis.

questions.text: Regarding yellow fever:

options.A: Transmission is through man handling contaminated monkey meat
options.B: Routine immunization is done for children at 6 months in Baringo county
options.C: The vaccine is contraindicated in pregnant women
options.D: It is a non – haemorrhagic virus

questions.explanation: The vaccine is contraindicated in pregnant women (C) is the best answer because yellow fever vaccine is a live attenuated vaccine, which is avoided in pregnancy (and in severe immunosuppression, infants under 6 months and egg allergy) unless the risk of infection is high. Transmission through handling contaminated monkey meat (A) is incorrect because the virus is spread by the bite of infected Aedes (and Haemagogus) mosquitoes, and monkeys are a reservoir. Routine immunisation at 6 months in Baringo county (B) is incorrect because the WHO routine schedule for yellow fever vaccine is at 9 months, and a 6-month schedule could not be confirmed. It is a non-haemorrhagic virus (D) is incorrect because yellow fever is a viral haemorrhagic fever (fever, jaundice, bleeding and kidney failure). Note: some references call the pregnancy restriction a precaution rather than an absolute contraindication, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: Presence of worms migrating across the conjunctiva/ eye are characteristic of infection with:
questions.explanation: Loa loa (B) is correct because the African eye worm (spread by the Chrysops deer fly) causes adult worms that migrate through the subcutaneous tissue and across the conjunctiva, which can be seen, together with transient Calabar swellings; it is treated with diethylcarbamazine or albendazole. Onchocerca volvulus (A) is incorrect because it causes river blindness through microfilariae in the eye and skin nodules (spread by the blackfly), but the worms are not seen crossing the conjunctiva. Wuchereria bancrofti (C) is incorrect because it causes lymphatic filariasis (lymphoedema and elephantiasis). Dracunculus medinensis (D) is incorrect because it is the Guinea worm, which emerges through a skin ulcer, mainly in the legs.

questions.text: In cholera:

options.A: The cases are referred to the main hospitals for proper management
options.B: Breastfeeding is contraindicated to prevent trans-mammary transmission
options.C: Health workers need to notify the disease surveillance and response unit
options.D: One gets infected when consuming water contaminated with trophozoites

questions.explanation: Health workers need to notify the disease surveillance and response unit (C) is correct because cholera is a notifiable disease under the International Health Regulations, so a suspected case is reported immediately to the sub-county disease surveillance and response coordinator, so that the outbreak can be investigated and controlled. The cases are referred to the main hospitals (A) is incorrect because cases are managed at the nearest facility or cholera treatment centre, with rehydration started at once. Breastfeeding is contraindicated (B) is incorrect because breastfeeding is encouraged to continue. Contaminated water with trophozoites (D) is incorrect because the cause is Vibrio cholerae, a bacterium, and trophozoites belong to protozoa such as Entamoeba histolytica and Giardia.

questions.text: The leadership theory that proposes that leaders are born and made is:
questions.explanation: Trait theory (B) is the best answer because it proposes that effective leaders have certain personal traits (intelligence, self-confidence, integrity, drive and sociability), some of which are inborn and some can be developed through experience and training, so leaders are both born and made. Great man theory (C) is incorrect because it holds that leaders are born and cannot be made. Quantum leadership theory (A) is incorrect because it describes leadership in a complex, changing, interconnected system. Servant leadership theory (D) is incorrect because it states that the leader's first aim is to serve the followers. Note: this item is open to interpretation, so check it against the marking scheme.

questions.text: The organization structure that form from a narrow span of control is:
questions.explanation: Tall (B) is correct because a narrow span of control (each manager supervises few staff) requires many levels of management to cover the whole organisation, which gives a tall (hierarchical) structure with close supervision but slower communication. Flat (A) is incorrect because a wide span of control gives few management levels. Circular (C) and functional (D) are incorrect because they describe other organisational designs (for example the circular design places the leader at the centre, and the functional design groups staff by specialty), and are not determined by the span of control.

questions.text: A problem-solving technique that managers utilize to reduce or eradicate a problem from occurring in the future is:
questions.explanation: Root cause analysis (C) is correct because it is a systematic method (using tools such as the five whys and the fishbone diagram) of finding the underlying cause of a problem or incident, so that corrective action addresses the cause and prevents the problem from recurring. The 80/20 rule (A) is incorrect because the Pareto principle helps to prioritise the few causes that produce most of the effects. Trial and error (B) is incorrect because it tries solutions at random, and does not identify the cause. Brainstorming (D) is incorrect because it is a way of generating ideas, and does not itself find the cause.

questions.text: The level of management whose main role is to formulate the vision of the organization is:
questions.explanation: Top level managers (D) is correct because the top managers (for example the board, the chief executive and directors) set the vision, mission, goals and strategic direction of the organisation, and make the long-term policy decisions. Bottom managers (A) and first line managers (B) are incorrect because they supervise the day-to-day operations and the staff who do the work (for example ward in-charges). Middle level managers (C) is incorrect because they turn the strategies into operational plans and coordinate the departments.
